dialogs.text: Another quiet night. You sit at your computer, casually scrolling through emails—student newsletters, club updates, and the usual spam.
Then one subject catches your attention: 🚀 JOIN THE OPEN INNOVATION HACKATHON – BEGINNERS WELCOME!
A hackathon? You hover over the email, unsure whether you should open it.
The email opens. Bright colors and pictures of smiling participants fill the screen.
“Collaborate. Create. Innovate. Join the 48-hour Byteon Online Hackathon! Register now. Build from anywhere.”
An online hackathon? So… I don't even have to go anywhere?
The idea sounds exciting. But then another thought enters your mind. Hackathons always seemed like competitions for people who already knew what they were doing.
I don't think I'm ready for this.
You scroll past it. Then you scroll back. Something about the invitation keeps pulling you in.
After a moment, you sigh and click the email.
Suddenly, your screen flickers. A small blue orb appears in the center of your screen.
Hello! I see you're reviewing an invitation to the Byteon Online Hackathon.
Whoa! Who—or what—are you?
I'm Aira, your AI Resource Assistant. And it looks like you've received an invitation to your first hackathon.
My first? How do you even know that?
Because you're staring at the registration button like it's about to attack you.
Okay… maybe I am a little nervous.
That's normal. Most first-time participants feel that way.
But I'm not even a programmer.
Good thing hackathons aren't only for programmers.
Before you can respond, your screen fills with a bright blue light. When it fades, your room is gone.
You find yourself standing inside a strange digital world filled with glowing screens, floating icons, and endless lines of code.
Welcome to my digital learning space.
Think of it as a place where you can learn what you need to know before entering your first hackathon.
So this is some kind of simulation?
Exactly. And don't worry. No experience required.
But what if I don't have the skills?
Then you learn.
What if my idea isn't good enough?
Then you improve it.
And what if I don't know anyone?
Then you meet people.
A hackathon isn't simply a programming competition. It's a place where people with different skills work together to create something.
Let me show you.
Aira snaps her fingers. Holograms of different participants appear around you.
One person is coding. Another is designing an interface. Someone else is presenting an idea. Others are discussing problems and brainstorming together.
Look closely. None of them started as experts.
Everyone has a first hackathon. Some people make mistakes, some change their ideas halfway through, and some discover that their first plan doesn't work at all.
So… failing is okay?
Making mistakes is part of learning.
You don't join a hackathon because you already know everything. You join because you want to learn, create, and try something new.
You look around the holograms again. For the first time, the people on the screen don't look like unreachable experts. They look like people who were once beginners too.
Let's start with the basics.
A large registration screen appears in front of you.
First, you register for the hackathon and check its eligibility requirements.
A checklist appears.
Then you choose whether you'll work alone or with a team.
And if I don't have a team?
That's what the community is for.
A Discord interface appears.
This is where participants communicate during the event.
Several channels appear: #announcements, #team-formation, #help-desk, and #general-chat.
You can look for teammates, ask questions, follow announcements, or simply talk with other participants.
So Discord is basically the event headquarters?
Exactly.
Another screen appears with submission requirements, deadlines, judging criteria, and theme guidelines.
And before you start building, read the rules. Knowing the rules helps you understand what you need to accomplish.
Finally, a virtual stage appears with a countdown.
The opening ceremony is where organizers explain the theme, schedule, challenges, and other important information.
That actually sounds simpler than I expected.
See? You're already learning.
Now that you know how it works, tell me honestly. What's stopping you from joining?

choices.text: I'm afraid my ideas won't be good.

dialogs.text: Skills can be learned. You don't need to know everything before you begin.
You just need to be willing to learn along the way.
No idea starts out perfect.
Good ideas are developed through questions, testing, and improvement. Your first idea doesn't have to be your final idea.
That's exactly why hackathons have communities and team-formation channels.
You might arrive knowing nobody and leave having met people who share your interests.
You know what? You've learned enough for your first challenge.
A challenge?
You came here carrying a lot of assumptions about hackathons. Let's see how many of them are actually true.
Ready?
I think so.
The screen lights up: HACKATHON MYTH BUSTER.
Let's clear those myths one by one.

minigame.description: Aira gives you statements—decide if they're True or False to earn Confidence Points.

questions.tip: Hackathons need designers, storytellers, presenters, researchers—every skill matters!
questions.aira_reaction: Right! Hackathons thrive on diverse skill sets!

questions.statement: You must know advanced coding before joining.
questions.tip: Beginner-friendly hackathons expect learners. You learn faster by doing!
resources: No-Code Tools: Glide, Bubble, Figma Prototype Mode
questions.aira_reaction: Exactly! Everyone starts somewhere—even expert hackers began as beginners!

questions.tip: A simple prototype or even a mockup can demonstrate an idea.
questions.aira_reaction: Perfect! Prototypes don't have to be perfect!

questions.statement: If my idea isn't completely original, I shouldn't join.
questions.tip: Ideas can be improved, adapted, or personalized.
questions.aira_reaction: Nice! Innovation can come from improving existing ideas!

questions.statement: Hackathons are overly competitive and toxic.
questions.tip: Hackathons can provide opportunities for collaboration, learning, and community.
questions.aira_reaction: Correct! Collaboration is an important part of hackathons!

questions.statement: You must stay awake for 24–48 hours straight.
questions.tip: Taking breaks and getting enough rest can help you stay productive.
questions.aira_reaction: Exactly! Rest is important when working on a project!

questions.statement: Hackathons are about teamwork and creativity.
questions.tip: Communication and collaboration are important parts of hackathons.
questions.aira_reaction: Absolutely! Collaboration is an important hackathon skill!

questions.tip: Hackathons can welcome students, professionals, hobbyists, and beginners depending on their eligibility rules.
questions.aira_reaction: Yes! Different hackathons welcome different participants!

questions.statement: You need expensive equipment or top-tier devices.
questions.tip: The tools you need depend on the project and hackathon requirements.
questions.aira_reaction: Correct! You can start with the tools you already have!

questions.statement: If you don't win, you wasted your time.
questions.tip: Hackathons can provide experience, skills, connections, and portfolio pieces.
resources: How to Write a Hackathon Case Study
questions.aira_reaction: Exactly! The experience itself can be valuable!

achievement.title: Hackathon Myth Buster
achievement.description: Completed the first mini-game by busting common hackathon myths. Confidence boosted!

dialogs.text: Excellent! You busted the myths.
The digital world begins to fade.
The glowing screens disappear, and the familiar walls of your room slowly return.
Heh…
You look at the invitation again. The registration button is still waiting.
But something feels different now. The hackathon doesn't seem quite as intimidating as it did before.
I still don't know everything… but maybe I don't have to.
You don't need to be ready for everything. You just need to be willing to take the first step.
Your cursor moves toward the registration button. This time, you don't immediately pull away.
The fear hasn't completely disappeared. But now, there's something else beside it.
Curiosity. And maybe… a little confidence.
Tomorrow, we'll talk about teams.
Because even online… no one hackathons alone.
You close the uninstall window. For now, Aira stays.
And with one click, your first step into the hackathon world begins.

achievement.title: First Steps
achievement.description: Complete Chapter 1 of How to Hackathon
